summary: Each generator advance must produce one array value. Updating one saved index with constant-time modular arithmetic matches that per-yield lower bound.

optimality.argument: Every call to next must return one yielded value and therefore requires at least constant work. The generator performs a fixed number of arithmetic operations, one indexed read, one yield, and a constant-size state update regardless of array length or jump magnitude.

replacement_checks.evidence: Producing the required value for one generator advance necessarily performs at least one return or yield operation.
One advance normalizes the new index with two remainders and fixed additions, then reads and yields exactly one array element.
Authored cases cover positive, negative, zero, full-cycle, and extreme jumps; one-element arrays; boundary start indices; persistent state; and the maximum 100-step schedule.
